evals.prompt: How do I get my repo to 1000 stars?
evals.expected_output: Should reframe stars as a lagging popularity snapshot and point at forks, issues, and returning contributors as the real signals. Should audit the free permanent items first: topics, license, description, profile README, pinned repos. Should explain trending ranks velocity relative to the repo's own baseline, so promotion must concentrate on one day. Should give realistic timelines with the survivorship caveat.
assertions: Reframes stars versus forks, issues, and returning contributors
Checks topics and license before recommending promotion
Explains star velocity relative to baseline
Recommends concentrating all promotion on one day
Gives a realistic timeline (1-3 months with promotion)
Names the survivorship bias in star case studies

evals.prompt: My README is 900 lines with a full table of contents. Should I add more documentation to it?
evals.expected_output: Should say no and invert the request. The star decision happens in about 15 seconds in the first screenful; a long table of contents where a demo should be is the classic failure. Should prescribe cutting to roughly 120 lines with one category sentence, a demo GIF of 2-5 MB, a quick start in the first 200 words, four badges, and everything else moved to docs/.
assertions: Specifies a demo GIF in the first screenful with a size range
Specifies quick start within the first 200 words
Limits badges to a small functional set
